messages.subject: multiple indicators multiple group multiple cohort latent growth curve model
parts:
Hi all,


I want to estimate (comparable) growth linear curves for panel data with 5 waves, the problem being that I would have to define different slopes for each of the age cohorts to account for the fact that participants had different age at baseline (3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18; N= about 2500) See for Mplus https://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap6/ex6.18.html and see for theoretical discussion of the problem http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/10937321.  

Using    , group="ageATbaseline" does not allow me to specify 
that the slope is unique to each group (I have 6):

age 3 group: 
s =~ 0*mdss1 + 0.3*mdss2 + 0.8*mdss3 + 1.2*mdss4 + 1.8*mdss5

age 6 group:
s =~ 0.3*mdss1 + 0.8*mdss2 + 1.2*mdss3 + 1.8*mdss4 + 2.1*mdss5

age 9 group:
s =~ 0.8*mdss1 + 1.2*mdss2 + 1.8*mdss3 + 2.1*mdss4 + 2.4*mdss5 

... and so on...

So even though the issue is rather complex my questions are simple:
 How do I specify a model for each group separately? (Know how it looks like in, like in Lisrel or Mplus.
 And is it possible to obtain an overall solution across models?


Many thanks,
Henrik

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: multiple indicators multiple group multiple cohort latent growth curve model
parts: I would have to define different slopes for each of the age cohorts to account for the fact that participants had different age at baseline (3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18; N= about 2500)

So you are running a multiple-group model, where the different age cohorts are the different groups, but every cohort has a fixed schedule?  This is way simpler than defining a different schedule for each individual, as Mehta & Neale were describing (which is not available in lavaan).  You are fitting the same model in each group, but you are just fixing the loadings to different time-values in each group.  See the lavaan tutorial for how to do this:  http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

age 3 group: 
s =~ 0*mdss1 + 0.3*mdss2 + 0.8*mdss3 + 1.2*mdss4 + 1.8*mdss5

age 6 group:
s =~ 0.3*mdss1 + 0.8*mdss2 + 1.2*mdss3 + 1.8*mdss4 + 2.1*mdss5

age 9 group:
s =~ 0.8*mdss1 + 1.2*mdss2 + 1.8*mdss3 + 2.1*mdss4 + 2.4*mdss5 

... and so on...
How do I specify a model for each group separately?

Assuming these are the only three groups, it would look like this:

s =~ c(0, 0.3, 0.8)*mdss1 + c(0.3, 0.8, 1.2)*mdss2 + c(0.8, 1.2, 1.8)*mdss3 + c(1.2, 1.8, 2.1)*mdss4 + c(1.8, 2.1, 2.4)*mdss5

And you can easily extrapolate to more age cohorts by putting more fixed values in the vectors.
And is it possible to obtain an overall solution across models?

What is an "overall'' solution?  Every group will have their own estimates of the mean and variance of the linear slope.  If you want to see whether the slope is the same across groups, then you can constrain that parameter to equality by using the same label across the 6 cohorts:

s ~ c(slope, slope, slope, slope, slope, slope)*1

Also described in the lavaan tutorial:  http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
